novel_features.name: Time-windowed new articles
novel_features.description: Show NEJM articles first seen in your local corpus within a time window.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local first-seen timestamps; NEJM offers no 'what's new since' API.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs only what changed since the last check, not the whole issue.

novel_features.name: Current-issue reading digest
novel_features.description: Triage the current issue grouped by specialty or type with abstracts and free/paywalled flags.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local join across issue articles and their enriched metadata; the site has no digest view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to summarize the week's NEJM issue in one structured payload instead of fetching each article.

novel_features.name: Personal reading list
novel_features.description: Queue NEJM articles by DOI locally and track read/unread state.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local mutable per-user state the logged-out website lacks.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to persist a clinician's to-read queue across sessions without an account.

novel_features.name: Specialty and type trends
novel_features.description: Show how NEJM output distributes by specialty, article type, and issue across the synced corpus.
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregation across the local corpus (and across repeated syncs over time).
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to quantify NEJM coverage patterns no single page exposes.

novel_features.name: Open-access finder
novel_features.description: Surface free full-text NEJM articles in the corpus, newest first.
novel_features.rationale: Requires enriched isFree flags filtered locally; the website buries free full-text.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for unsubscribed readers who can only act on freely-readable articles.

narrative.headline: Browse, search, and triage New England Journal of Medicine articles from the terminal, backed by a local corpus and a browser-compatible transport that clears Cloudflare.
narrative.value_prop: NEJM has no public API. This CLI turns its public surfaces into an offline-queryable, agent-native corpus: the current issue and recently-published feeds, per-article abstracts and metadata by DOI, and full-text search over everything you have synced. Novel local-state commands like 'since', 'digest', 'reading-list', 'trends', and 'open-access' do things the website and PubMed wrappers cannot.
narrative.auth_narrative: No account or API key is required for the public surfaces this CLI uses (RSS feeds and server-rendered article metadata). Full article text remains subscription-gated on nejm.org; the CLI reports a free/paywalled flag and never circumvents the paywall.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the CLI is wired and NEJM is reachable via the Surf transport.
Pull the current issue and recently-published feeds into the local store.
List the current issue's articles with authors and pages.
Offline full-text search over the synced corpus.
Fetch one article's abstract and metadata by DOI.

troubleshoots.fix: Run 'nejm-pp-cli sync' first to populate the local store.
Run 'nejm-pp-cli sync --enrich' or 'nejm-pp-cli article get <doi>' to fetch detail-page metadata.
The CLI uses Surf (Chrome-TLS) transport which clears Cloudflare; ensure you are on a current build.

troubleshoots.symptom: Live keyword search against nejm.org fails
troubleshoots.fix: NEJM's search endpoint is Cloudflare-hard; this CLI searches the local synced corpus instead. Sync more issues to widen coverage.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or clinician needs current peer-reviewed NEJM literature metadata programmatically: the current issue, recently published articles, an article's abstract and bibliographic data by DOI, or an offline searchable corpus filtered by specialty, type, author, or free-access. It is the right choice when you want structured, composable output without driving a Cloudflare-gated browser.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to read full article text behind the NEJM paywall; it surfaces abstracts and metadata only.
Do not use it for a broad multi-journal literature review; use a PubMed/Crossref tool for cross-journal search.
Do not use it for live keyword search of the entire NEJM archive; it searches only the locally synced corpus.
